study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Loreto et al., Alzheimer's & Dementia: Diagnosis, Assessment & Disease Monitoring, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Alzheimer's disease heterogeneity revealed by neuroanatomical normative modeling

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Apply neuroanatomical normative modeling to a real-world clinical cohort with biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer's disease to map individual-level cortical thickness deviations, quantify total outlier count, and examine associations with phenotype, disease stage, depressive symptoms, and amyloid burden.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The main text states the reference cohort (n=33,072) pooled from public datasets and the adaptation dataset (n=20) scanned at the same site. Supplementary Table 1 lists representative datasets (ABCD, Cam-CAN, CNP, FCON, HCP, OASIS3, PNC, TOP, UKBB).
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: The reference cohort consisted of a group of 33,072 cognitively normal adults pooled from publicly available neuroimaging datasets... The adaptation dataset consisted of a group of 20 cognitively normal (CN) older adults who had an MRI scan at ICHT for research purposes. Supplementary Table 1: Demographic breakdown of the datasets... ABCD; Cam-CAN; CNP; FCON; HCP; OASIS3; PNC; TOP; UKBB.

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Visual QC by three authors; common errors at skull stripping (75%) and intensity normalization (25%) corrected via parameter adjustment, control points, and manual edits; 2 patients excluded after repeated failures.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression with partial pooling; site/batch-specific parameters drawn from shared priors; adaptation with site-matched controls to recalibrate parameters; avoids separate harmonization (e.g., ComBat).
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: HBR... incorporates structural dependencies among model parameters by sharing a common prior... calculates z-statistics to account for both additive and multiplicative batch effects, obviating the need for data harmonization.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Region-wise z-scores relative to normative range; outliers defined as z < -1.96; total outlier count (tOC) = sum of outlier regions per subject.
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: Method section defines z-score threshold and tOC.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: z-scores of < -1.96 were defined as outliers... The total outlier count was calculated by summing the number of outlier regions for each patient.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: ANCOVA (covariates: age, sex) for group differences in tOC by sex, phenotype (amnestic vs non-amnestic), and disease stage (MCI vs dementia); Pearson correlation between tOC and age; linear regression of tOC vs amyloid SUVR; Hamming distance to quantify within-group dissimilarity; standard case–control comparisons (ANCOVA for mean thickness; region-wise t-tests with FDR).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Cortical atrophy patterns in biomarker-confirmed AD are highly heterogeneous with the superior temporal sulcus most frequently outlying; higher total outlier counts occur in non-amnestic and more advanced cases and are negatively associated with amyloid burden.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Median tOC was 21.5 (IQR 35), ranging 1–120 across 148 ROIs. STS had the highest outlier proportion (lh 52%, rh 60%), with 48% of patients showing bilateral STS outliers. tOC was higher in AD-dementia vs MCI-AD (median 30 vs 17.5; F(1,82)=8.33, p=0.005) and in non-amnestic vs amnestic (median 37.5 vs 19.5; F(1,81)=5.49, p=0.02). Females had higher tOC than males (median 31.5 vs 17.5; p=0.002). tOC correlated negatively with amyloid burden (SUVR) and mean cortical thickness was lower in clinical AD vs ADNI controls (F(1,154)=88.78, p<0.001; region-level: 104/148 regions thinner).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Outlier thresholding at z < -1.96 and summarizing tOC provide an interpretable individualized marker; spatial outlier maps and Hamming distance capture heterogeneity beyond case–control averages.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Relatively small clinical sample; scanner and field-strength mismatch between clinical (1.5T) and adaptation (3T) datasets may introduce noise; retrospective clinical data limited granularity (cognition, depression); no subcortical normative outliers modeled; need to assess spatial dependencies and explore connectivity-informed normative models.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Eighteen externally scanned patients were excluded by the model; extensive FreeSurfer QC with manual edits performed. HBR-based transfer learning used site-matched controls for calibration. No explicit EV/MSLL or probabilistic calibration metrics reported; software package not stated. Subcortical normative modeling not included.
